We are informed that at the beginning of the month of 
January this year a group of several persons was planning an 
attempt on the life of an important member of the U. S. S. Re 
Embassy, apparently against Mr. De. V. Bogomoloff, the 
Ambassador. The group was directed by a man named Siline 
alias Jack Martin, residing at No. 346 North Chekiang Road 
(Chapei). His accomplices were two Koreans who had arrived 
from Hongkong and a Chinese. The attempt was to have been 
made on February 24,

in which Ivoline was to remain to await a telephone message 
informing him of the wiconee or failure of the attempt. In 
either case, Ivoline was to communicate the information 
immediately to Chichkine by telephone No. 75700.

had failed. He thereypon transmitted the information to

Date March 26, 1934

Subject (in full) Alleged attempt to assassinate Mr. D. V. Bogomoloff,
Soviet Ambassador to China.

Made by D.S.I. Golder. Forwarded by J.B.Ru. D.I.

With reference to my report on the above subject dated
March 23, 1934.
It was learned that a similar report as made to this office
was made to the French Police who have been kind enough to supply
us with a copy thereof (report and translation attached). The
information contained in the French Police report on the matter
is substantially the same as ours. In paragraph 3 of their
report they make mention of telephone No.73700 which was alleged
to be situated at an address where Shishkin was waiting for
information from Ivolin. Enquiries into the name of the holder
of the telephone reveal that no such number is at present in
operation. This fact points out more clearly that the whole
scheme is a fabrication and has no foundation in fact.
The French Police conclude, as do we, that the persons
concerned in the "alleged plot" are to a man, in the pay of the
Soviet Intelligence Service and that A. Sokoloff is working for
both the Soviet and the Japanese Intelligence services.

Em Golder
D. S. I.

关于我于1934年3月23日就上述主题提交的报告。

Organization of an Attempt on the Life of D. V. Bogomoloff,

Organisation d'un attentat contre D.V. BOGOMOLOFF, Ambassadeur de
l'URSS en Chine

Nous sommes informés de ce qu'au début du mois de Janvier dernier un groupe de plusieurs personnes avaient l'intention d'organiser un attentat contre la vie d'un membre influent de l'Ambassade de l'URSS, apparemment contre Mr. D.V. BOGOMOLOFF, Ambassadeur. La bande aurait été dirigé par le nommé SILINE alias Jack MARTIN, habitant au No. 346, North Chekiang road (Chapei). Ses complices auraient été deux coréens arrivés de Hongkong et un Chinois. Cet attentat devait être perpétré vers le 24 Février dernier. Les agisseurs de cette terreur auraient été surveillés par un autre groupe composé des nommés E.K. SIRNIS (No. 125, Baikal road), P. CHICHKINE, ancien agent de la Police Chinoise de Harbine, A. SOKOLOFF (No. 23, Linda Terrace) et D.V. IVOLINE (No. 6 passage No. 1003, Avenue Joffre). Le 24 Février, CHICHKINE aurait informé IVOLINE qu'on pouvait s'attendre à l'exécution de l'attentat de jour en jour et l'aurait envoyé au No. 19, Tiendong road, où était loué par CHICHKINE et SIRNIS une chambre et où IVOLINE devait rester en attendant un coup de téléphone, l'informant du succès ou de l'insuccès de l'attentat. Dans les deux cas, IVOLINE devait communiquer immédiatement la nouvelle à CHICHKINE par téléphone No. 73700. Le même soir, à 22 heures, IVOLINE avait été informé par téléphone par un inconnu que l'affaire était manquée. Il avait transmis ensuite cette information à P. CHICHKINE.

Il est à noter que les deux groupes en question - celui des "terroristes" et celui chargé de les surveiller - comprennent plusieurs membres fortement soupçonnés d'être des agents à la solde de l'URSS, tels que le nommé SILINE alias Jack MARTIN - chef du groupe chargé de l'attentat contre BOGOMOLOFF, E.K. SIRNIS et A. SOKOLOFF, membres du 2ème groupe chargé de surveiller les agissements de SILINE et de ses complices. A. SOKOLOFF est soupçonné, en outre de travailler simultanément pour le compte des services de renseignements japonais./.

ground or first floor, facing Tiendong Road.    The room had no

Ivolin then left the premises and returned to his home at 1003
Avenue Joffre, (Room 3).

have heard nothing further of the plot.    On the latter dates
reference was made to the affair by the local press.

to the whole affair being in the nature of a faked plot engineered
by Jack Silin and his satellites with the object of compromising
Japan in the eyes of the world, as that Power would, in all
possibility, have been accused of having promoted the undertaking.
Local White Russians were also to have been drawn into the affair
and to ensure that this would be properly contrived, Sokoloff,
with the help of Masaloff, sought admittance as members of the

然而，调查显示，1934年2月24日，伊沃林通过北苏州路的一个入口被带入河滨大厦，在经过多条走廊后，最终被引至底层或一楼的一间面向天潼路的房间。房间内无人居住。他被独自留下，被告知等待电话。上午10点左右，电话响起，伊沃林接听，一个他无法辨认声音的人告诉他，刺杀博戈莫洛夫的行动失败了。随后伊沃林离开该处，返回其在霞飞路1003号（3室）的住所。

经调查查明的事实表明，整个事件本质上是由杰克·西林及其追随者策划的一场伪造的阴谋，目的是在世界面前损害日本的声誉，因为日本极有可能被指控推动了这一行动。当地的白俄人也本将被卷入此事，为确保这一安排得当，索科洛夫在马斯洛夫的帮助下，试图加入位于霞飞路1008号的“青年俄罗斯协会”（Mladorossy），随后提议该组织采取一些积极行动。

sell information of the plot to any one of the foreign Intelligence

据推测，该阴谋的另一目的是将有关该阴谋的情报出售给在上海活动的任何一家外国情报机构。事态本会如此安排，以便让泽尔尼塞（Zernise）居功，声称是他发现了该阴谋。
显而易见，如果激起各情报机构好奇心的计划得以成功实施，实际上并不打算让苏联公使受到伤害；但是，一旦他们出售情报的计划未能达到目的， conspirators（阴谋者）完全有可能转而对付他们的雇主——苏联政府。
对据称为此案积极参与者的背景进行仔细调查后，揭示出一个有趣但重要的事实：杰克·西林（Jack Silin）、K. 泽尔尼塞（K. Zernise）、A.A. 索科洛夫（A.A. Sokoloff）和 I.N. 马萨洛夫（I.N. Masaloff）均已知与苏联情报机构有关联。此外，据悉，杰克·西林和 K. 泽尔尼塞与一名叫 I.I. 安加尔斯基（I.I. Angarsky）的人有直接接触，据说此人负责国家政治保卫总局（G.P.U.）在上海的活动，且西林曾在数年前协助其从日本逃往澳大利亚。

China Press March 14 1934.

Plot On Bogomoloff
Life Denied By Consul

Milikovsky Avers Hangchow
Trip Never Planned

The report of an alleged assassination attempt on Mr. Dimitri Bogomoloff, Russian ambassador to China, published in the Nichi Nichi Shimbun, local Japanese daily, was branded as pure fabrication by Mr. M. V. Milikovsky, Russian vice-consul in Shanghai, in an interview given Chinese press representatives yesterday.

The report as carried in the Nichi Nichi Shimbun alleges that two Russians and two Chinese, dressed in Japanese clothes, waited at North Station to kill Mr. Bogomoloff on February 28 when the Russian ambassador was scheduled to leave Shanghai for a pleasure trip to Hangchow. The latter, the report alleged, received advanced information and cancelled the trip.

It was pointed out at the Russian Consulate General yesterday that Mr. Bogomoloff had never planned to visit Hangchow. Mr. I. T. Splivanek, Russian consul general, went to Hangchow last week shortly after his arrival here but nothing happened to him during the trip.

The Russian Embassy issued a statement denying the report and stating that no such plot ever existed. The embassy further stated that Mr. Bogomoloff is now in Nanking on official business and will return to Shanghai shortly.

Sensational report by the "Shanghai
Nichi-Nichi Simbun" on the intended attempt
on the life of Soviet Ambassador D.V. Bogomoloff.
----------------

Sensation of the day yesterday was a report which
appeared in the local daily Japanese newspaper the "Shanghai
Nichi-Nichi Simbun" on the alleged intended attempt on
the life of Soviet Ambassador to China D.V. Bogomoloff.
According to the "Shanghai Nichi Nichi Simbun" the
attempt was to take place late in the evening, on Saturday
February 24, when the Soviet Ambassador D.V. Bogomoloff
was planning to leave Shanghai for Hangchow, for a few days'
rest.
According to the information received by the Japanese
newspaper, four extremists were waiting the arrival of D.V.
Bogomoloff at the North Station with a view to throwing a
bomb at the Soviet Ambassador and if necessary to fire
several shots straight at him.
The Japanese newspaper states that D.V. Bogomoloff
was given a warning about the intended attempt on his life
and postponed his journey to Hangchow.
It is interesting to recall that in the Autumn of last
year an alleged attempt had already been made on the life
of Soviet diplomats and Bogomoloff in particular, when
a bomb was thrown in the courtyard of Soviet Embassy in
Sinza Road. Police investigations at the time, however,
failed to confirm any attempt. The damage done by the
explosion of the bomb was very slight. It resulted only
in a small hole in the shape of a funnel being dug out
in a flower-bed of the Embassy's garden. There were no
fragments of the bomb found by police in the courtyard of the
Embassy.

昨日的轰动性新闻是本地日文日报《上海日日新闻》刊登的一篇报道，称有人 allegedly（据称）意图刺杀苏联驻华大使 D.V. 博戈莫洛夫。

ВТОРНИК 19 МАРТА 1934 ГОДА № 2622.

СЕНСАЦИЯ „ШАНХАЙ НИЧИ-НИЧИ СИМБУН“
О ГОТОВИВШЕМСЯ ПОКУШЕНИИ НА
СОВ-ПОСЛА Д. В. БОГОМОЛОВА.

Сенсацией вчерашняго дня явилось сообщеніе мѣстной ежедневной японской газеты «Шанхай Ничи Ничи Симбунъ» о подготовлявшемся, якобы, покушеніи на жизнь совѣтскаго посла въ Китаѣ Д. В. Богомолова.

Какъ сообщаетъ «Шанхай Ничи-Ничи Симбутъ», покушеніе должно было быть проведено въ жизнь позднею вечеромъ, въ субботу 24 февраля когда совѣтскій посолъ Д. В. Богомоловъ намѣревался выхать изъ Шанхая въ Ханьчжао, на нѣсколько дней для отдыха.

По полученнымъ японской газетой свѣдѣніямъ, къ моменту ожидавшагося прибытія на Сверный вокзалъ Д. В. Богомолова — тамъ находились четверо террористовъ, которые должны были бросить бомбу въ сов-посла, а въ случа необходимости, произвести въ него, въ упор, нѣсколько выстрѣловъ.

Однако, сообщаетъ яп-газета, Д. В. Богомоловъ получилъ свѣдѣнія о подготовляющемся на него покушеніи, и отмѣнилъ свою поѣздку въ Ханьчжао.

Интересно напомнить, что осенью прошлаго года, было сдѣлано якобы, одно покушеніе на жизнь совѣтскихъ дипломатовъ и Богомолова въ частности, когда во дворъ совѣтскаго посольства, на Синва род была брошена «бомба».

Однако, произведенное полиціей тщательное разслдованіе тогда, не установило факта покушенія. Поврежденія отъ взрыва «бомбы» были незначительны. Была выбита небольшая воронка на клумбѣ въ саду посольства. Никакихъ осколковъ отъ «бомбы» во дворѣ посольства обнаружено полиціей не было.

刺杀苏联公使未遂案

苏联政府最近针对远东局势变得非常活跃，关注远东的各列强正特别留意苏联的活动。经查，苏联国家政治保卫局（G. B. W.）正计划秘密实施一项严重的阴谋。

据《日日新闻》收到的消息，苏联国家政治保卫局驻上海负责人组织了一个情报局，以调查某个特定国家，并任命麦克·苏希利尼斯（Mack Sushilinise），别名达里尼斯（Darinis），为该局局长。苏联国家政治保卫局驻上海负责人组织了一个恐怖团伙，并任命杰克·马丁·希林（Jack Martin Shiline）（拉脱维亚人）领导该团伙，雇佣白俄和朝鲜人执行刺杀任务。

该团伙最初意图于2月24日在北站刺杀即将前往杭州的苏联驻华公使博戈莫洛夫（BOGOMOLOFF）先生。苏联公使获悉该计划后，取消了杭州之行。

根据收到的有关该计划的情报，安排由恐怖团伙头目希林（Shiline）负责，雇用两名俄国人和两名姓王和李的男子，在北站刺杀苏联公使。他们将被要求穿上某国的服装，并被指示供认受雇于某国，以便使该国与苏俄之间的关系变得危急。这一事件将使世界相信该国扰乱世界

Jack Silin, alias Martin, alias Silinsky, alias
Johnsen, alias Gilin, alias Sihle, (File I.O. 9123), is
a Latvian, about 51 years of age, residing at 346 North
Chekiang Road. He is a notorious swindler, confidence
man and narcotic and arms dealer (Ser. No.72). He took
part in the revolutionary movement in the Russian Baltic
Provinces and was a member of the Terrorist Group which
pillaged several estates from their German landlords and
is reported to have killed a Police official. Silin was
arrested and sentenced to death but upon his sentence
being commuted to life imprisonment, he was then sent
along with other convicts to construct roads in the Amur
Province of Soviet Russia. He managed to effect his
escape with a number of other convicts after killing
several of the guards. He was next heard of in Japan
where he remained for some time, but while there he
assisted I.I. Angarsky (at present in charge of G.P.U.,
activities in Shanghai) in escaping from Japan to
Australia. Silin later made his way to the U.S.A. but
was deported because of his Bolshevik activities. He
then went to Australia where he remained for 9 years
working as a miner and as a professional wrestler.
From 1919 to 1925 it is known that he became a
dealer in cocaine, opium and other narcotics, trading
between Shanghai and Harbin. In 1926, he went to Hankow
and took part in the Bolshevik activities there. He
acted for some time as advisor to General Wu Pei Fu, who,
according to report, was at that time being supported by
the U.S.S.R. in the war with Chang Tso Lin. Whilst in
Hankow, Silin and certain wealthy Chinese dealt in
contraband goods with an office on Avenue Dubail, French
Concession, Hankow. In April, 1927 he returned to

杰克·西林（Jack Silin），别名马丁（Martin）、希林斯基（Silinsky）、约翰森（Johnsen）、吉林（Gilin）、西勒（Sihle），（档案号 I.O. 9123），是一名拉脱维亚人，约51岁，居住在浙江北路346号。他是一个臭名昭著的骗子、诈骗犯以及毒品和军火商（序列号72）。他曾参与俄国波罗的海省份的革命运动，并且是从德国地主手中掠夺多处庄园的恐怖小组成员的一员，据报还杀害了一名警察官员。西林被捕并被判处死刑，但在刑期减为无期徒刑后，他被与其他罪犯一起派往苏俄阿穆尔省修筑道路。他在杀死几名看守后，设法与其他一些罪犯一起逃脱。随后有关于他在日本的消息，他在那里停留了一段时间，但在此期间，他协助I.I.安加尔斯基（I.I. Angarsky）（目前负责格别乌在上海的活动）从日本逃往澳大利亚。西林后来前往美国，但因布尔什维克活动被驱逐出境。随后他去了澳大利亚，在那里呆了9年，从事矿工和职业摔跤手的工作。
从1919年到1925年，已知他成为可卡因、鸦片和其他麻醉品的经销商，在上海和哈尔滨之间进行贸易。1926年，他前往汉口，并参与了那里的布尔什维克活动。他曾一度担任吴佩孚将军的顾问，据报道，当时苏联在与张作霖的战争中支持吴佩孚。在汉口期间，西林与某些富有的中国人在法租界杜拜尔路（Avenue Dubail）的一个办事处从事违禁品交易。1927年4月，他返回

During his stay here he admitted being a communist.
In June, 1927, he disappeared from the above boarding

he was arrested by the French Police for concealing a

No.8 How Fok Terrace, but was released before the case

October, 1928, Silin left Shanghai for Tientsin and Peking
accompanied by his paramour, Mrs. Mayoroff, a dancing
partner by profession who was formerly employed at Hankow
and subsequently at the Alcazar Cafe at Shanghai. Under
the Esthonian name of Sihle, Silin embezzled $2,000 from
his Chinese business partner at Tientsin and escaped to
Shanghai in April, 1929. In Shanghai, he occupied Room
No.4 in the Savoy Hotel until May 4, 1929, when he again
disappeared leaving unpaid an account of $20. He later
resided for some time at No.182 Alcock Road in the room
occupied by a friend named Stoss. At about this time,
he opened an Import and Export Office under the name of
Tampico Trading Company at No.216 Szechuen Road, Room 204.
In the beginning of August, 1929, Silin closed this office,
leaving the rent unpaid. In 1933, Silin worked as a coal
mine expert to a wealthy Chinese named Loo or Liu, owner
of a Coal Mine near the Tai Hu Lake. It is reported that
one M.S. Prostoff (File D-1625) was also connected with
this enterprise.

In recent years it was suspected that he had become
a G.P.U. agent engaged in propaganda work amongst British
and French soldiers.

It is said that Silin is in receipt of a pension
from the U.S.S.R. Government as an ex-political convict.

1927年6月，他从上述寄宿处失踪，留下200美元的账单未付。1927年10月，他因在霍福台8号（How Fok Terrace）的住所内藏匿一名法国殖民地部队逃兵而被法国警察逮捕，但由于缺乏证据，在案件提交法庭之前被释放。1928年10月，西林在其情妇梅奥罗夫夫人（Mrs. Mayoroff）的陪同下离开上海前往天津和北京，梅奥罗夫夫人是一名职业舞伴，此前曾在汉口受雇，随后在上海的阿尔卡萨咖啡馆（Alcazar Cafe）工作。西林使用爱沙尼亚名字西勒（Sihle），从其在天津的中国商业伙伴那里侵吞了2,000美元，并于1929年4月逃回上海。在上海，他住在萨伏伊酒店（Savoy Hotel）4号房间，直到1929年5月4日，他再次失踪，留下20美元的账目未付。后来他在奥尔科克路182号一位名叫斯托斯（Stoss）的朋友所住的房间里居住了一段时间。大约在此时，他在四川路216号204室以坦皮科贸易公司（Tampico Trading Company）的名义开设了一家进出口办事处。1929年8月初，西林关闭了该办事处，留下租金未付。1933年，西林为一位姓陆或刘的富有中国人担任煤矿专家，此人是太湖附近一处煤矿的所有者。据报道，一名M.S.普罗斯托夫（M.S. Prostoff）（档案号 D-1625）也与该企业有关联。

近年来，有人怀疑他已成为格别乌（G.P.U.）特工，在英国和法国士兵中进行宣传工作。

据说西林作为前政治犯，正在领取苏联政府发放的养老金。

P.P. Shishkin (File No.3170 and D-2255) is a Russian.
He claims to have been in the employ of the Japanese Secret
Service from 1918 to 1924. He later went to Manchuria and
became a member of the Communist Party, eventually rising to
tje important post of Secretary to the Trade Unions. At the
same time he acted as a secret informer to the Chinese
Political Police in Harbin and upon the rupture of diplomatic
relations between Russia and China in 1929 he began to work
openly for the Chinese Police and took part in the arrest of
numerous communists and Soviet citizens. An attempt was
made on his life by communist terrorists the same year.
In May, 1930 Shishkin came to Shanghai from Harbin
and published a book entitled "Bolshevism in China."
Apparently, the book did not prove a financial success for
Shishkin began to be involved in monetary difficulties and
had eventually to secure work as an informer to the French
Police and to certain members of the Shanghai Municipal
Police. During the Sino-Japanese hostilities in the
neighbourhood of Shanghai in 1932, Shishkin contracted
for the supply of Russian labour to the Japanese military.
Shishkin's connections with Zernise, Jack Silin
alias Martin and Stoessel began some time in 1933. It
was Zernise who supported him. Recently Shishkin had a
quarrel with Zernise and he joined Silin and Stoessel.
A report is current that Shishkin has been attempting
to dispose of certain documents relating to the activities
of the Brotherhood of Truth (an active anti-Bolshevik body)
and the transportation of arms from Japan for the use of
terrorists, but no prospective buyers have yet come forward.
Shishkin resides at No.54 Nanking Road.

P.P. 希什金（P.P. Shishkin）（档案号3170和D-2255）是一名俄国人。他声称在1918年至1924年间受雇于日本特务机关。后来他去了满洲，成为共产党成员，最终升任工会秘书的重要职位。同时，他担任哈尔滨中国政治警察的秘密线人，并在1929年俄中外交关系破裂后开始公开为中国警察工作，参与逮捕了许多共产党员和苏联公民。同年，共产主义恐怖分子曾试图刺杀他。
1930年5月，希什金从哈尔滨来到上海，出版了一本名为《中国的布尔什维主义》的书。显然，这本书并未在财务上取得成功，因为希什金开始陷入金钱困境，最终不得不受雇于法国警察和上海公共租界工部局警务处的某些成员担任线人。在1932年上海附近的中日敌对行动期间，希什金承包向日军供应俄国劳工。
希什金与泽尔尼斯（Zernise）、杰克·西林（别名马丁）和斯托塞尔（Stoessel）的联系始于1933年的某个时候。是泽尔尼斯支持了他。最近希什金与泽尔尼斯发生争吵，转而加入了西林和斯托塞尔一方。目前有传言称，希什金一直试图处理某些文件，这些文件涉及真理兄弟会（一个活跃的反布尔什维克团体）的活动以及从日本运输武器供恐怖分子使用的事宜，但尚未出现潜在的买家。希什金居住在南京路54号。

Emelian Adrianovitch Kolemeetz alias Kolomietz
was born at Kiev, South Russia, in 1880. He came to
the notice of the Shanghai Municipal Police in 1924 as
a Bolshevik propaganda agent employing three agents named
Ivan Mascheriakoff, Ivan Samsonoff and Ismail Amiroff.
The first two named were engaged in communist propaganda
work among the white Russian community, while the last
named was sent to Hongkong in an effort to influence
the Chinese people against foreigners. In September,
1924, he lived at No.41 Dixwell Road where he had many
visitors, mostly Indians and Japanese, among the latter
being one H. P. Shastri, a contributor to the "Asia
Review," member of the Swaragi Party and leader of the
Hindustani Association in Shanghai. Kolomietz later
established an office on North Szechuen Road above the
Marco Polo Cafe where he handled the repatriation of
white Russians to the U.S.S.R. Prior to his coming
to Shanghai, Kolomietz was in Japan for a time.
It is said that Kolomietz is at present planning
with one Grasin to publish a Russian newspaper to be
known as the "Segodnia."
Kolomietz is residing somewhere in the French
Concession.

埃梅利安·阿德里亚诺维奇·科列梅茨（Emelian Adrianovitch Kolemeetz），别名科洛米耶茨（Kolomietz），1880年出生于南俄基辅。他于1924年进入上海公共租界工部局警务处的视线，当时他是一名布尔什维克宣传特工，雇佣了三名分别名为伊万·马谢里亚科夫（Ivan Mascheriakoff）、伊万·萨姆索诺夫（Ivan Samsonoff）和伊斯梅尔·阿米罗夫（Ismail Amiroff）的特工。前两人从事在白俄社区中的共产主义宣传工作，而最后一人被派往香港，试图影响中国人民反对外国人。1924年9月，他居住在狄思威路41号，那里有很多访客，大多是印度人和日本人，其中包括H. P. Shastri，他是《亚洲评论》（Asia Review）的撰稿人、斯瓦拉吉党（Swaragi Party）成员以及上海印度斯坦协会（Hindustani Association）的领导人。科洛米耶茨后来在北四川路马可波罗咖啡馆（Marco Polo Cafe）楼上设立了一个办事处，处理白俄遣返至苏联的事宜。在来到上海之前，科洛米耶茨曾在日本停留过一段时间。
据说科洛米耶茨目前正与一名格拉辛（Grasin）计划出版一份名为《今日》（Segodnia）的俄文报纸。
科洛米耶茨现居住在法租界的某处。

ALEXEY Alexevitch Sokoloff is a Russian, born in 1908.
He went to Harbin during the revolution in Russia. When
China and Russia broke off diplomatic relations in 1929,
Sokoloff joined the Chinese Police. It is not known
when he left that service, but he is reported to have
been in America for a time from which country he was
deported for his boot-legging activities. He proceeded
to Harbin via Shanghai.
During 1933 he worked with the Japanese Military
Mission as an intelligence agent in the course of which
he made several trips to Russia in connection with his
work. He was subsequently suspected of being a Soviet
spy to secure information about Japanese activities in
Manchuria. Sokoloff began to find his position
untenable and fled to Shanghai in August, 1933. Upon
arrival here, he approached the Mladorossy, a Russian
monarchist organization, and threw out strong hints
that that organization should take up some active work.
Upon receiving a warning regarding Sokoloff, the
Mladorossy refused to have anything further to do
with him.
Sokoloff is residing with his friend Masloff
at No.23 Linda Terrace, Avenue Joffre.

阿列克谢·阿列克谢耶维奇·索科洛夫（Alexey Alexevitch Sokoloff）是俄罗斯人，生于1908年。俄国革命期间，他前往哈尔滨。1929年中俄断交时，索科洛夫加入中国警察队伍。其离职时间不详，但据报他曾一度在美国停留，后因从事私酒贩卖活动被该国驱逐出境。他经上海前往哈尔滨。

1933年间，他作为情报人员为日本军事代表团工作，在此期间因工作需要数次前往俄罗斯。随后，他被怀疑是苏联间谍，旨在获取有关日本在满洲活动的情报。索科洛夫开始感到处境难以为继，遂于1933年8月逃往上海。抵沪后，他接触了“青年俄罗斯党”（Mladorossy，一个俄罗斯君主主义组织），并强烈暗示该组织应开展一些积极行动。在收到关于索科洛夫的警告后，“青年俄罗斯党”拒绝再与他有任何往来。

索科洛夫现与其朋友马斯洛夫（Masloff）同住于霞飞路林达里23号。

pages.en:
Illarion Nikolaevitch Masloff is a Russian of
about 38 years of age. During the civil war in Siberia
he served in the White Army and later with the Military
Intelligence Service at Nikolsk Ussuriysk. In 1933,
he joined the Manchukuo or Japanese Intelligence Service
at Harbin. About the middle of September, he received
a letter from Sokoloff inviting him to Shanghai. Upon
arrival here, Masloff approached the Russian Legitimist
Monarchist Organization and carried out some intelligence
work for that body. He was trusted for he had produced
documents and certificates regarding his former service.
Like his friend Sokoloff, Masloff claims to be in the
employ of the Japanese Intelligence Service at Harbin
and that his wages are remitted to him regularly through
the Thriftcor Bank.
Masloff is occupying room No.23 Linda Terrace,
Avenue Joffre, where he receives numerous visitors.
pages.zh:
伊拉里翁·尼古拉耶维奇·马斯洛夫（Illarion Nikolaevitch Masloff）是俄罗斯人，年龄约38岁。西伯利亚内战期间，他在白军服役，后在乌苏里斯克（Nikolsk Ussuriysk）的军事情报部门任职。1933年，他在哈尔滨加入了伪满洲国或日本情报机构。9月中旬左右，他收到索科洛夫的一封信，邀请他前往上海。抵沪后，马斯洛夫接触了俄罗斯正统君主主义组织，并为该机构从事了一些情报工作。由于他出示了有关其先前服役经历的文件和证书，因而获得了信任。与其朋友索科洛夫一样，马斯洛夫声称受雇于哈尔滨的日本情报机构，并称其薪水通过 thriftcor 银行（原文如此，可能指某储蓄银行）定期汇给他。

马斯洛夫现住霞飞路林达里23号房间，此处访客众多。
